23	point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
24	locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
25	commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.
26	
27	Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
28	complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
29	12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine

32	## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)
33	
34	* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
35	  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
36	  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
37	  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
38	  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
39	  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
40	  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points

42	  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
43	  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and

94	/-! ## §1. Finite-module transport along a semilinear additive equivalence
95	
96	The elementary bookkeeping lemma for moving `Module.Finite` across the
97	section comparisons of the fromSpec dictionary: a surjective-semilinear
98	additive equivalence transports finite generation. -/
99	
100	/-- **`Module.Finite` descends along a surjective-semilinear additive
101	equivalence.**  If `e : M ≃+ N` intertwines the `R`-action on `M` with the
102	`S`-action on `N` through a surjective ring homomorphism `σ : R →+* S`
103	(`e (r • x) = σ r • e x`) and `N` is a finite `S`-module, then `M` is a
104	finite `R`-module: the preimages of a finite `S`-generating set generate
105	`M` over `R`, because every `S`-scalar lifts along `σ`. -/
106	theorem Module.Finite.of_addEquiv_semilinear {R S : Type u} [Semiring R] [Semiring S]
107	    {M N : Type u} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module S N]
108	    (σ : R →+* S) (hσ : Function.Surjective σ) (e : M ≃+ N)
109	    (he : ∀ (r : R) (x : M), e (r • x) = σ r • e x) (hN : Module.Finite S N) :
110	    Module.Finite R M := by
111	  obtain ⟨n, w, hw⟩ := hN.exists_fin (R := S) (M := N)
112	  refine Module.finite_def.mpr (Submodule.fg_def.mpr
113	    ⟨⇑e.symm '' Set.range w, ((Set.finite_range w).image _), ?_⟩)

Measured on 2026-07-27 for `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`
(see [[workspace-orientation]], [[deumbrella-cascade-and-self-matching-pkill]]).

**Build cost.** From-scratch `lake build` (wiped `.lake/build`, Mathlib from the shared package
cache): **43:15 wall, 9.7 GB peak RSS, 8,723 jobs green**, on 16 cores contended with another
workspace run. It is **critical-path bound, not throughput bound** — 113 of 165 modules finish
inside 10 minutes and the last 33 minutes are an almost serial chain (`GlueDescent` gates
`SerreTwist`/`GrassmannianQuot`/`QuotFunctorDef`/`RigidPushforward`, which gate the Adelic tail);
for most of that stretch exactly one job runs, so more cores buy nothing. Heaviest modules
(completion minus last dependency completion): QuotScheme 804s, TensorObjSubstrate 538s,
GlueDescent 504s, Adelic/NonconstantToP1 453s, GrassmannianZariskiSheaf 385s.

The cost driver is the bare `import Mathlib`: measured on a 49-line module, **16.6s / ~7 GB with
the umbrella vs 3.5s / 2.0 GB with four precise imports**. At 7 GB per process a 62 GB host
sustains ~8 concurrent jobs, not 16. Trimming `maxHeartbeats` ceilings saves no compute by
construction — the levers are imports and splitting the oversized modules.

**The strategy fact that matters most.** The blueprint and roadmap advertise the
Grassmannian → Quot → flattening → Pic route, but `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`
(2026-07-09) already chose route "D3 Milne–Kollár" instead, and says verbatim "Off-path and
untouched: Quot-lane sorries". `FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550` marks `HasSmoothProperQuotient`
"PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH"; `Scheme.QuotScheme` has zero consumers. Only ~375 Lean lines are
exclusive to the Quot endgame (the rest of QuotScheme/QuotFunctorDef/GradedHilbertSerre is
imported by the committed route), but an 8,434-line blueprint chapter describes a dead lane.

**Two truth caveats on "153 sorry-free modules".** It is a *local* claim: `instHasPicScheme`
(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:317`) is `⟨sorry⟩` on a global instance — sole producer of
`HasPicScheme`, 41 use sites — and `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
(`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:163`) likewise, so both leak through

In the AJCR Rebuild the roadmap node summaries are long, confident, and **frequently wrong about
the Lean**. On 2026-07-25 a six-front recon (one agent per blocking front) with an *independent
adversarial refuter per front* overturned or materially corrected claims on 4 of 6 fronts —
including "C9 is independent of the DD-R lane" (false: it needs a `DivRepGlobalData` producer,
of which there are zero) and "`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` is the cheapest real advance"
(false: bare `Prop`, zero producers, pinned mathlib avatars don't apply). The refuters also
corrected the *recon agents* on 3 of 6 fronts.

**Why:** these summaries are written by sessions under time pressure and are never re-verified;
they accumulate. Planning directly on them wastes whole rounds.

**How to apply:** before committing to work the roadmap describes, run recon → adversarial
verify, and require file:line evidence for every load-bearing claim. Budget for it — the pass
above took ~35 min wall-clock and paid for itself immediately. Do the same to your *own*
conclusions: an adversarial pass on my proposed repair found three real defects and one hard
blocker I had missed. See [[workspace-orientation]], [[lane-orchestration]].

**The specific mechanism behind half the false "MISSING" claims** (found 2026-07-27): a session that
is killed mid-flight leaves its files uncommitted, and the orchestrator's `workspace[NNNN rM] …
integrate …` commit sweeps them into HEAD under a message that names no file. So the file IS in HEAD
and IS rooted, but `git log --oneline -- <path>` shows only the integrate commit, and the round's own
documents — written before the integration — say the declaration does not exist. In round 5 this had
`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md` calling link L11 "MISSING, never attempted" while
`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` sat in HEAD with a fresh `.olean` implementing half of it. **Check the
working tree and `.olean`s, not the prose, and treat any file added by an `integrate` commit as
work the record does not describe.**

Related recurring hazard: the **shared git index goes stale** whenever a lane commits via the
mandated private-index+CAS recipe (files the lane just added show as `D ` staged deletions
against the new HEAD). It is harmless *until* someone commits from the shared index, which
would record spurious deletions. Fix is one line:
`git --git-dir=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD`. Check
`git status --porcelain | grep '^D'` before finishing a session. This has now bitten at least
twice (see the run-0048 session-0002 report).

metadata:

Two operational gotchas learned the hard way on 2026-07-27 while converting the AJC project's
bare `import Mathlib` to precise imports (see [[workspace-orientation]]).

**1. The de-umbrella cascade.** In `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, 35 of 164 modules
carry **no Mathlib import at all** — they inherit the whole library transitively from a parent.
Narrowing a parent silently strips the library from every such dependent that actually used
something from it: wave 1 narrowed 27 DAG sources and broke 4 dependents with 124 errors
(`StructureSheafAb`, `FiniteGaloisQuotient`, `GrassmannianQuot`, `Pic0TangentSpace`), then one
more (`StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf`) on the next round.

**Why:** a module's minimal-import probe is only correct once its whole transitive project closure
is umbrella-free, and a module that imports no Mathlib of its own is invisible to that test —
nothing in its own text says it needs the library.

**THE ORDERING RULE (learned the expensive way).** Bottom-up is right for *probe correctness* —
a module's minimal imports cannot be computed until everything beneath it is clean — but it is
WRONG for *net progress* whenever the module has a cone of import-less dependents above it.
Narrowing `Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf.lean` stripped the library from nine modules
in the `StructureSheafModuleK → Genus → Jacobian` chain: net −1 bare, +9 bare. Over wave 2,
converting 8 modules forced 25 back onto the umbrella and the day's count went 39 → 64.
**Give a module's import-less dependents their own precise imports FIRST (top-down within the
cone), then narrow the parent.** Each dependent then holds its own imports and nothing below can
strip it.

**Find the exposure before converting, not after.** The at-risk set is computable from the import
graph alone: modules with no `import Mathlib*` line of their own whose transitive project closure
contains no bare module. Elaborate all of them in parallel with `lake env lean` (which reads the
built oleans and never writes `.lake/build`, so it is safe alongside a running build) — 54
candidates resolved in minutes, versus one 10–30 minute full build per victim discovered in
dependency order, because lake stops at the first failure in a chain and never reaches downstream.
Of the 54, only 24 actually needed Mathlib; the other 30 were loading 1.79 GB of oleans for
nothing and are pure wins.

**How to repair:** give the broken dependent a bare `import Mathlib`, restoring exactly the
environment it used to inherit — deterministic and cannot fail. `scripts/deumbrella-wave.sh` now
does this automatically per wave (`build_and_repair`, up to 4 attempts) and refuses to start the
next wave until the current one is green. Also expect some modules to resist narrowing outright:
`GrassmannianQuot.lean` times out at `isDefEq`/`whnf` at the default 200k heartbeats *with*
precise imports but builds fine with the umbrella — a smaller environment can send a defeq check
down a different, slower path, so every conversion must re-elaborate and revert on failure.

**A conversion's verification is only valid against the import graph as it stood at that moment.**
`Genus.lean` converted and verified green in wave 1, then broke in wave 2 when something beneath
it was narrowed. Nothing is settled until the whole tree is converted.

**2. Self-matching process patterns.** `until ! pgrep -f "deumbrella.sh"; do sleep 15; done`

  audit failure mode is real and flatness does *not* rescue it: membership
  of an overlap section in the `u`-lattice `im σ₁` bounds no `t`-degree of
  any particular representation over the `t`-ladder, because ladder
  representations are not unique (the chart modules are merely *spanned*
  by the ladder, never freely).  Base-flatness of `M` is irrelevant to this

  (`x`-)torsion.

  direct proof secretly re-runs the same window difficulty: an element of

  generators without kernel control.

  01YS/EGA III 3.2.1 run a *descending induction on cohomological degree*:
  choose a surjection `E := ⊕ᵢ O(-dᵢ) ↠ M`, with kernel `K`; then

     generation for ℙ¹, with no sheaf theory.

85	## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard
86	
87	Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
88	seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
89	then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
90	plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
91	The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
92	you did not ask for:
93	
94	- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
95	  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
96	  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
97	  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:
98	
99	  ```bash
100	  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
101	  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
102	  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
103	  ```
104	
105	- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
106	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.
107	
108	At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
109	since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
110	blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):
111	
112	```bash
113	"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
114	"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
115	```
116	
117	If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
118	working tree, commit once.
119	
120	## Reading history / a project's diff
121	
122	Run from the workspace root:
123	
124	```bash
125	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
126	
127	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
128	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
129	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
130	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
131	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
132	```
133	
134	Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
135	`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
136	run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:
137	
138	```bash
139	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
140	  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
141	```
142	
143	To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
144	the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
145	commit changed).
146	
147	## Caveats
148	
149	- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
150	  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
151	  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
152	  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
